Marginal means (average predictions)

Source: R/effects.R
marginal_means.Rd

The prediction averaged over rows, overall or with every row set to each value of a covariate (counterfactual or g-computation marginal means, as avg_predictions(variables = ) of marginaleffects). Unlike the estimated marginal means of emmeans, which average over a balanced reference grid, these average over the observed rows.

Usage

marginal_means(
  object,
  variable = NULL,
  at = NULL,
  type = c("mean", "parameter", "link"),
  par = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  re = c("conditional", "zero"),
  level = 0.95,
  vcov = "model",
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted model.

variable

Covariate to set, or NULL for the overall average.

at

Values of the covariate; its levels (or mean and the mean plus and minus one standard deviation for a numeric covariate) by default.

type

"mean" (the predicted mean), "parameter" (a distribution parameter) or "link" (its linear predictor).

par

Distribution parameter for type = "parameter" or "link".

newdata

Rows to average over; the analysis rows by default.

re

"conditional" (with the estimated random effects) or "zero" (random effects set to zero).

level

Interval level.

vcov, ...

Covariance choice for frequentist fits (see vcov.regcomp_fit()).

Value

A data frame with one row per value.

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(300), g = factor(sample(c("a", "b"), 300, TRUE)))
d$y <- rpois(300, exp(0.2 + 0.5 * d$x + 0.4 * (d$g == "b")))
marginal_means(regcomp(y ~ x + g, family = "poisson", data = d), "g")
#>   g estimate std_error statistic      p_value    lower    upper
#> 1 a 1.449369 0.1009556  14.35651 9.699538e-47 1.251500 1.647238
#> 2 b 2.023168 0.1137642  17.78388 9.422775e-71 1.800194 2.246142
